column1: # user_yes vocabulary (v2.7 D3/D4 prototype, reworked after the grill F4/F24).  Data, not code.
# kind<TAB>lang<TAB>python regex (matched case-insensitive on the owner text)
# kinds (a `yes` alternation lists longer words first: leftmost-first match):
#   yes      a short affirmative; anchored at the start of the owner text
#   hold     any hit anywhere vetoes a yes and a direct intent; riders
#            (but / except / only / -man / ppaego) and temporal deferrals
#   inspect  any hit vetoes a direct intent (asking to SEE, not to DO)
#   act      an imperative-action token; a direct intent needs one
#   cls:<c>[/<verb>]  path B (direct intent) object phrase for class <c>; a
#            service phrase names its verb (R2-4: restart never covers
#            bootout / disable / kill / self-update; user_yes.PATH_B_VERBS).  Only
#            service, baseline and owner-file have one (user_yes.PATH_B_CLASSES):
#            destructive / push / tag / release / gate-switch are path A only
#            (the exact command shown, then the owner's next turn says yes).
#            A phrase names the OBJECT, never a bare class verb: no
#   procedure  owner-file lint (D4 HF23): IMPERATIVE rule / procedure forms
#            only ("always answer ...", "항상 표로 답해"), never a fact that
